intro: Uruguay is a small, stable democracy between Argentina and Brazil that won the first ever football World Cup.

chapters.title: Charrúa and colonists
text: The Charrúa people lived here when Europeans arrived. Portugal founded Colonia del Sacramento in 1680, and Spain founded Montevideo in 1724, making the land a battleground between the two empires.

chapters.title: Independence
text: José Gervasio Artigas led early resistance. Uruguay became independent in 1828 as a buffer state between Brazil and Argentina.

highlight.title: Artigas
highlight.text: He is honoured as the father of the nation.

chapters.title: Democracy and reform
text: In the early 1900s President José Batlle y Ordóñez created one of the world's first welfare states. A military dictatorship ruled from 1973 to 1985. Since then Uruguay has been one of the most democratic countries in the Americas.

timeline.title: Cannabis law
timeline.text: First country to legalise it nationally.

keyTerms.meaning: A small country between two larger rivals.
A government that provides health care, pensions and more.
